answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate is severe and non-negotiable. Memory c4 shows renegotiation recovered margin but was against an incumbent; memory c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. However, at 94% line utilization with no buffer, switching carries execution risk. Memory c2 demonstrated that moving to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Verifying c2 confirms the low-cost vendor path is operationally viable. Given the 14-day expiration, renewing (c1) or deferring (c5) neither addresses the 18% cut mandate. Adding a second source (c3) would not hit the cost target. Switching to the proven low-cost vendor from c2 is the only action that can plausibly achieve the 18% reduction while maintaining supply continuity, though the tight timeline and high utilization create execution risk. Standard experiment scaling validates the vendor under production conditions before full commitment.
